headline: Approved Saddlebrook site lighting revision on Allentown Road; continued Grassy Rd. earth removal applications to September 21, 2026.
summary: Speakers addressed vape and smoke shops and data centers, and members scheduled a special meeting on both for August 20, 2026. Members approved a site lighting revision for Saddlebrook on Allentown Road, with one condition. They continued four Grassy Rd. earth removal applications to September 21, 2026, and set a public hearing on a change of zone at Lot 101 Terryville Avenue.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the July 13, 2026 meeting, 5-0.
Accepted Application #2571 for a change of zone at Lot 101 Terryville Avenue and set a public hearing for September 21, 2026, 5-0.
Accepted Application #2572 and moved it to New Business on the same agenda, 5-0.
Scheduled a virtual special meeting for August 20, 2026 at 5:00 PM on vape/smoke shops and data centers, 5-0.
Continued four Grassy Rd. earth removal applications (#2567, #2568, #2569, #2570) to September 21, 2026, 5-0.
Approved the Saddlebrook site lighting revision with a condition that the lighting plan not be signed off until staff comments are addressed, 5-0.

Bristol Zoning Commission Regular Meeting of August 10, 2026 
– 1 – 
 
 
BRISTOL ZONING COMMISSION MINUTES 
MONDAY AUGUST 10, 2026 
By: Acting Chairman Goodwin Time: 6:00 P.M. Place: City Hall 
111 North Main St. 
Council Chambers 
First Floor 
 
ROLL CALL: 
 
MEMBERS NAME PRESENT ABSENT 
    
REGULAR MEMBERS: David White (Chairman) X  
 Richard Goodwin (Acting Chairman) X  
 John LaFreniere (Secretary) X  
 Richard Harlow X  
 Sara Mangiafico X  
    
ALTERNATE MEMBERS: Peter Caruso X  
 Morris Patton X  
 Jeffrey Hayden X  
    
STAFF: Robert M. Flanagan, AICP, City Planner X  
 Brandon Peate X  
 
1. Call to Order 
Per the order of Acting Chairman Goodwin, the meeting wascalled to order at 6:00 P.M. 
Acting Chairman Goodwin reminded the Commission the next regular meeting is Monday, September 21, 2026. 
2. Pledge of Allegiance 
3. Public Participation 
Acting Chairman Goodwin explained if any public audience are in attendance to speak on the Grassy Rd. applications 
the public would be able to speak after the applications are opened. The Acting Chairman said the public audience 
may speak on any Public Participation not associated with public hearings at this time. 
The following persons had concerns under Public Participation with the following items on this evening’s agenda: 
6. City Council Referrals 
a. Vape/Smoke Shops 
Marco Palmeri, Director of Bristol Burlington Health District, 240 Stafford Ave.; Dr. Thomas Ward, 125 South Down 
Dr. and Mayor Ellen Zoppo-Sassu, 47 Kory Lane, with Councilman Mark Dickau, on Zoom. 
Mr. Palmeri gave a brief presentation on tobacco and vape shops with a health standpoint with tobacco, vape and 
electronic delivery systems. The director requested a prohibition on these facilities and new facilities. Mr. Palmieri’s 
view was to cap or prohibit new licenses and approvals for new facilities. The director reviewed the statistics noting 
there were 30 existing businesses. Mr. Palmeri said Bristol had to consider whether it wanted and excess of 
businesses with an addictive use to young persons. 
 
The director added the City had to consider a reasonable number of facilities because space was limited for customer 
bases. Mr. Palmeri noted Public Act 26-8, §53, effective October 1, 2026 and Public Act 26-100, §33, effective 
January 1, 2027 recognized the need to enforce and monitor the facilities.
Bristol Zoning Commission Regular Meeting of August 10, 2026 
– 2 – 
 
 
Dr. Ward supported a moratorium because these facilities do not support the health of young persons. The resident 
suggested the ordinance be revised because it is not substantial enough. Dr. Ward noticed many of the facilities on 
Farmington Ave. have illegal signage particularly near the Giamatti Center because Bristol was family oriented. 
Mayor Zoppo-Sassu read into the record a letter dated August 7, 2026, from the Economic and Community 
Development Commission, regarding Vape/Smoke Shops. Mayor Zoppo-Sassu said the Economic and Community 
Development requested a moratorium for the Vape/Smoke Shops at their August 6, 2026, meeting. 
Mayor Zoppo-Sassu indicated there would be community outreach for amendments before the October 1, 2026 
effective date of Public Act 26-8, §53. The mayor supported a moratorium to prevent an influx of new facilities 
because there were 53 pending/inactive applications. 
a. Data Centers 
The following persons spoke against the data centers: Sarah Patano, 52 Irving St.; Shelly Mastroianni, 120 Sixth St.; 
Marco Palmeri, Director of Bristol Burlington Health District, 240 Stafford Ave.; Mayor Ellen Zoppo-Sassu, 47 Kory 
Lane in conjunction with Councilman Mark Dickau who was on Zoom. 
 
Ms. Patano explained she attended a City Council meeting that discussed data centers. The resident was unaware of 
a proposed data center until the Inland Wetlands Agency approved an application. Ms. Patano reviewed some 
research on data centers that showed negative health effects. Ms. Patano played a audio clip of the noise from a 
data center that would be similar in the downtown area. 
 
Ms. Mastriani inquired of the purpose, benefits and risks of data centers in Bristol. Ms. Mastriani had concerns of the 
chemicals used that may affect waterways. The resident added there may be complex issues affecting air quality. Ms. 
Mastriani was worried of conflicting Regulations and enforcement with the Inland Wetlands Agency, ConnDEEP and 
the Zoning Commission. The resident noted the C.G.S. 32-3, Pilot Program, means payment in lieu of taxes. 
Mr. Palmeri stated as a public health official he believed there would be public health impacts from data centers that 
needed consideration particularly near residential areas. The director noted data centers can run 24 hours/365 days a 
year. Mr. Palmeri noted there would be noise, substantial electrical demand, increased traffic, backup generator 
emissions and significant heating and cooling. The director agreed there would be impacts that were not well 
investigated for the community but should be considered. 
 
Mayor Zoppo-Sassu explained many of the current city officials, when elected, were unaware of the proposed data 
center on Riverside Ave. but were now reviewing the concerns with data centers. The mayor encouraged the 
Commission to adopt a text amendment to limit data centers over 15,000 sq. ft. Mayor Zoppo-Sassu verified the City 
Council does not have authority over the fuel cell which is proposed for Riverside Avenue. Mayor Zoppo-Sassu 
verified that the Staff of the Water and Sewer Dept. reviewed the water usage and technical items and were satisfied 
including a stop gap protection shutoff plan to protect residents. 
 
Ms. Fulton was in favor of the discussion that was at the City Ordinance Committee and supported a moratorium. 
The following persons had questions regarding Application #2572 under Public Participation: 
Karina Smith, 413 East St., Plainville, representing the Somak Property Management for the Saddlebrook Unit Owners 
Association; Thomas Martucci, 107 Terryville Lane and Joseph Longo, 59 Brookview Circle. 
 
Ms. Smith acknowledged the application was to bring the site into compliance but there were outstanding comments 
on the light poles. The property manager said the proposed light poles are the existing poles on site. 
Thomas Martucci, 107 Terryville Lane, agreed with the same concerns of Somak Property Management, regarding 
the light poles. The resident was concerned why the original plan could not be met. Mr. Martucci inquired why an 
alternative plan was being reviewed. 
 
Mr. Longo expressed concerns on the lighting not working at times. The resident said washer were placed under the 
lighting pads because the light poles/pads were out of square. Mr. Longo inquired if partial amounts or all the light 
poles would be replaced. The resident inquired if the light pole styles would be similar.
Bristol Zoning Commission Regular Meeting of August 10, 2026 
– 3 – 
 
 
Acting Chairman Goodwin closed Public Participation. 
4. Approval of Minutes 
 
a. Regular Meeting — July 13, 2026 
 
Acting Chairman Goodwin designated regular Commissioners White, Harlow, LaFreniere, Mangiafico and Goodwin to 
vote on the July 13, 2026, special meeting minutes. 
 
MOTION: Move to approve the minutes of the July 13, 2026, regular meeting. 
 
By: Harlow Seconded: Mangiafico. 
 
For: White, Harlow, LaFreniere, Mangiafico and Goodwin. 
Against: None. 
Abstained: None. 
 
5. Receipt of New Applications 
 
a. Application #2571 — Change of Zone from R-40 (Single-Family Residential) zone to I (General Industrial) 
zone at Lot 101 Terryville Avenue; Assessor's Map 61, Lots 101; Industrial Industries, LLC, applicant/owner. 
 
Acting Chairman Goodwin designated regular Commissioners Harlow, White, LaFreniere, Mangiafico and Goodwin to 
vote on Application #2571. 
MOTION: Move that Application #2571 be accepted and scheduled for a Public Hearing for the 
September 21, 2026, Regular meeting of the Zoning Commission. 
By: Harlow Seconded: Mangiafico. 
 
For: Harlow, White, LaFreniere, Mangiafico and Goodwin. 
Against: None. 
Abstained: None. 
 
The application is scheduled for public hearing. 
 
b. Application #2572 — Revision to an Approved Site Plan for Saddlebrook (Site Lighting Revision for 
Brookview Circle & Boulder Court) at Lot 14 Allentown Road; Assessor's Map 9, Lot 14; R-25/OSD (Single- 
Family Residential/Open Space Development) zone; Fragola Enterprises, LLC, applicant/owner. 
 
Acting Chairman Goodwin designated regular Commissioners Harlow, White, LaFreniere, Mangiafico and Goodwin to 
vote on Application #2572. 
 
MOTION: Move that Application #2572 be accepted and moved to New Business on tonight’s meeting agenda of 
the Zoning Commission. 
 
By: Harlow Seconded: Mangiafico. 
 
For: Harlow, White, LaFreniere, Mangiafico and Goodwin. 
Against: None. 
Abstained: None. 
 
The application is moved to New Business on tonight’s meeting agenda.
Bristol Zoning Commission Regular Meeting of August 10, 2026 
– 4 – 
 
 
6. City Council Referrals 
a. a. Vape/Smoke Shops 
b. Data Centers 
Acting Chairman Goodwin designated regular Commissioners Harlow, White, LaFreniere, Mangiafico and Goodwin to 
vote on City Council Referrals. Mr. Flanagan suggested a virtual special meeting of the Zoning Commission on 
August 20, 2026. 
MOTION:  Move to schedule a Special Meeting (via Online/Zoom) for August 20, 2026 at 5:00 PM to provide 
for a Commission discussion on the following City Council Referral’s for: 
 
a. a. Vape/Smoke Shops 
b. Data Centers 
 
By: Harlow Seconded: Mangiafico. 
 
For: Harlow, White, LaFreniere, Mangiafico and Goodwin. 
Against: None. 
Abstained: None. 
 
The applications are scheduled for a special meeting. 
 
Acting Chairman Goodwin noted the Public Participation would be allowed at the special meeting. 
 
7. Public Hearings 
 
a. Application #2567 — Special Permit for Earth Removal in excess of 400 cubic yards associated with the 
development of a residential dwelling lot at Grassy Rd. (Lot 214); Assessor's Map 20, Lot 214; R-40 (Single- 
Family Residential) zone; H&T Holdings of Bristol, LLC, applicant. 
 
b. Application #2568 — Site Plan for Earth Removal in excess of 400 cubic yards associated with the 
development of a residential dwelling lot at Grassy Rd. (Lot 214); Assessor's Map 20, Lot 214; R-40 (Single- 
Family Residential) zone; H&T Holdings of Bristol, LLC, applicant. 
 
c. Application #2569 — Special Permit for Earth Removal in excess of 400 cubic yards associated with the 
development of a residential dwelling lot at Grassy Rd. (Lot 216); Assessor's Map 20, Lot 216; R-40 (Single- 
Family Residential) zone; H&T Holdings of Bristol, LLC, applicant. 
 
d. Application #2570 — Site Plan for Earth Removal in excess of 400 cubic yards associated with the 
development of a residential dwelling lot at Grassy Rd. (Lot 216); Assessor's Map 20, Lot 216; R-40 (Single- 
Family Residential) zone; H&T Holdings of Bristol, LLC, applicant. 
Acting Chairman Goodwin explained Applications #2567, #2568, #2569 and #2570 would be heard concurrently but 
voted on separately. 
 
Acting Chairman Goodwin designated regular Commissioners Harlow, White, LaFreniere, Mangiafico o to vote on 
Applications #2567, #2568, #2569 and #2570. 
 
Attorney James Ziogas, 104 Bellevue Avenue, representing the applicant, explained the property lines were revised 
on the existing lots to make the lots at least 40,000 sq. ft. to become more conforming. The attorney specified the 
intention was to construct single family houses on Lot 214 and Lot 216. Attorney Ziogas noted the initial applications 
were to remove 145,000 cu. yds. materials. The attorney said the adjacent 6-acre lot was sold to the City to increase 
the Hoppers area versus developing the lot.
Bristol Zoning Commission Regular Meeting of August 10, 2026 
– 5 – 
 
 
Attorney Ziogas reviewed the plan brought to the Planning Commission to remove 4,500 cu. yds. materials from Lot 
216 and 2,100 cu. yds. materials from Lot 214 that was significantly reduced. The attorney said these lots were 
existing so there were no limits of clearing the trees. 
Attorney Ziogas described how the applicant worked with the Bristol Burlington Health District (BBH District) to 
remove 2,100 cu. yds. of debris. The attorney said there were no cesspools found. Attorney Ziogas verified there is 
1,600 cu. yds. of materials stockpiled to be taken off the two lots that would take about 3 months. The attorney 
noted the applicant worked with the Health District on the wells and septic system plan. 
Attorney Ziogas summarized the plan had less material to be removed than was proposed at the Planning 
Commission meeting. The attorney’s view was the site would be improved with this plan. Attorney Ziogas reviewed 
the photographs of the site. 
 
Attorney Ziogas noted the applicant received an approval from the Inland Wetlands Agency. The attorney stated 
there were a few areas on the properties to be cleaned up. 
 
Commission inquiries: Attorney Ziogas added that 400 cu. yds. of materials was removed from the site but in January 
2027 an additional 400 cu. yds. may be removed from the site. The attorney reported the applicant wanted to finish 
the plans because there are clients that wanted to purchase the properties. Attorney Ziogas verified the street would 
be extended, paved and improved. 
 
Acting Chairman clarified that the public audience may either speak during this meeting or at the next meeting 
because the applications would likely be continued. The Acting Chairman said at the next meeting the public 
audience may only speak if the public had new information. 
No one else spoke in favor of the application. 
The following person spoke against the applications: Michelle Rudy, representing Friends of the Hoppers-Birge Pond 
Nature Preserve (Friends of the Hoppers), 102 Henderson St. 
Ms. Rudy was pleased the applicant sold the 6 acres to the City to add to the Hoppers property because it was 
important to preserve. Ms. Ruddy did not know the larger volume of materials to be removed was reduced to 1,600 
cu. yds. Ms. Rudy read into the record the Friends of the Hoppers comments. The representative read into the record 
the technical reasons of the Friends of the Hoppers goal to preserve the area on all 4 borders extending beyond the 
boundaries of the site because it would affect the City. Ms. Rudy’s view was the plan went against the POCD, Zoning 
Regulations and Stormwater Regulations. 
 
The representative detailed how this plan would not only have ecological effects to this area but to different areas of 
the City by stormwater runoff and reduced soil filtration on the site. Ms. Rudy summarized how the new plan had no 
elements of the old plan and had to be reviewed again by the Inland Wetlands Agency. 
Ms. Rudy was concerned of preserving the hillsides that are gone with the existing excavation that exceeded the 400 
cu. yds. of materials. The representative had reservations on the effects on the existing and newly identified wildlife 
on the property with the plan. 
The attorney verified that the applicant would install tracking pads, silt fencing and sweep streets to prevent 
sediment. Attorney Ziogas was unsure if there would be sufficient ground water. The attorney said the 2,100 cu. yds. 
of debris needed to be removed but was filled with material from the stockpiles allowed in the Regulations. Attorney 
Ziogas added the applicant would request to remove the excess materials from the site. 
 
Acting Chairman Goodwin inquiries: the attorney agreed to grant a 10-day extension on the application on behalf of 
the applicant to get to the September Zoning meeting. 
Mr. Flanagan inquiries: Attorney Ziogas would work with Mr. Flanagan to amend the applications. 
 
MOTION: Move that Applications #2567, #2568, #2569 and #2570 be continued to the next Regular Meeting of 
the Zoning Commission on September 21, 2026. The applicant will need to grant a 10-day extension to 
keep the Public Hearing open.
Bristol Zoning Commission Regular Meeting of August 10, 2026 
– 6 – 
 
 
 
By: Harlow Seconded: Mangiafico. 
 
For: Harlow, White, LaFreniere, Mangiafico and Goodwin. 
Against: None. 
Abstained: None. 
 
The Applications #2567, #2568, #2569 and #2570 are continued. 
 
8. Old Business 
 
There was no old business. 
 
Item 9.a. New Business, Application #2572 was resumed at this time. 
 
9. New Business 
 
a. Application #2572 — Revision to an Approved Site Plan for Saddlebrook (Site Lighting Revision for 
Brookview Circle & Boulder Court) at Lot 14 Allentown Road; Assessor's Map 9, Lot 14; R-25/OSD (Single- 
Family Residential/Open Space Development) zone; Fragola Enterprises, LLC, applicant/owner. 
Acting Chairman Goodwin designated regular Commissioners Harlow, White, LaFreniere, Mangiafico and Goodwin to 
vote on Application #2572. 
 
Attorney Bryan Meccariello, 200 Executive Blvd., Southington, representing the applicant, reviewed the request to 
update the lighting plan for the property. Attorney Meccariello explained the applicant purchased the developer rights 
in December 2016. The attorney said the original condominium association was never funded so the owners at that 
time were not able to sell units. Attorney Meccariello said in the 2019 the units were reconfigured. 
 
The attorney indicated the plan is close to being finished. The attorney indicated the proposed plan was to install 10 
additional light poles and to replace the heads on the 10 existing light poles for a similar residential lighting style. 
Attorney Meccariello addressed the public participation concerns noting the grading and bases would be repaired. 
 
Richard Mace of Mace Electric, LLC, 125 Robert Jackson Way, Plainville, verified 2 of the light pole bases would be 
replaced. Mr. Mace explained the light poles would be replaced with 3000K residential lighting for reduced 
illumination. 
 
Scott Petrone, P.E. of R.R. Hiltbrand Engineering and Surveying, LLC, 225 North Main St., described the areas on the 
plans to be slightly amended while observing during recent rain storms. Mr. Petrone said he had a meeting with the 
Staff and condominium representatives. The engineer indicated with re-grading the slopes stormwater runoff had 
significantly improved during rain storms. The engineer agreed the outstanding Staff comments would be addressed. 
 
MOTION: Move that Application #2572 be approved with the following stipulations: 
1. The Lighting Plan shall not be signed off until all remaining staff comments have been addressed and 
the plan revised accordingly. 
By: Harlow Seconded: Mangiafico. 
 
For: Harlow, White, LaFreniere, Mangiafico and Goodwin. 
Against: None. 
Abstained: None. 
 
The application is approved. 
10. Staff Reports
Bristol Zoning Commission Regular Meeting of August 10, 2026 
– 7 – 
 
 
a. Zoning Report - July 2026 
Mr. Peate indicated this would be his last report with the City because he accepted a new position with another 
municipality. The Zoning Enforcement Officer reviewed his report dated August 5, 2026. The ZEO stated the Code 
Enforcement Office can enforce most of these items. 
11. Communications 
 
There were no communications. 
12. Adjournment 
Acting Chairman Goodwin designated regular Commissioners Harlow, White, LaFreniere, Mangiafico and Goodwin to 
vote on the adjournment. 
 
MOTION: Move to adjourn at 7:33 P.M. 
 
By: White Seconded: Mangiafico. 
For: Harlow, White, LaFreniere, Mangiafico and Goodwin. 
Against: None. 
Abstained: None. 
 
This meeting was recorded. 
Respectfully submitted, 
 
Nancy King 
Recording Secretary 
 
 
 
Richard Goodwin, Acting Chairman John LaFreniere, Secretary
